utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that's given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could I please have the usher's assistance in providing the witness with a document, please. It's bearing ERN N006-4901.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take a look at that piece of paper before you, and without saying the name out loud, please confirm that the information contained on the piece of paper is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, if the document could please be then shown to my learned colleagues and if there is no objection, I would ask to tender it under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P408, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the record, Your Honours, the Prosecution has now called Witness M-051.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you have been granted protective measures in the form of the use of a pseudonym and face distortion. Therefore, your face cannot be seen outside this courtroom and we will be referring to you as either Witness or Witness 051. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, drawing your attention to August, 2001 was the commander you reported to Commander Blazo Kopacev in the 1st Guardist Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And at that time, was the commander of the 3rd Guardist Battalion within the 1st Guardist Brigade named Major Mitre Despodov?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir, Witness M-051.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Give me a moment, Your Honours, please, to take the stand. To prevent interrupting the witness when he starts answering, we also prepared a binder with documents that we wish to show the witness so I would like to ask for the assistance of the usher in distributing those materials to the Chamber, to the witness and to the Prosecutor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-051, good afternoon. My name is Edina Residovic and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux, I appear for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Before I start asking you questions, I would like to ask you, Mr. M-051, to wait a while after you've heard my question for the question to be interpreted into Macedonian and into English, so that the Bench and the other colleagues in the courtroom are able to understand what I'm asking you and please only then answer the question I've asked you. Did you understand this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask to move into a private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the constitution and the law of the Republic of Macedonia you must be aware of this, the president of the republic is the commander in chief of the army in both the states of war and the state of peace. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Correct, he is the commander in chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you know, and you did know also, that the deployment of police forces during a war, in a state of war, is also decided such decision would be made by the president of the -- of the republic as a supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Correct. In cooperation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although in 2001 a new law on defence was adopted you could agree with me if I say that the president of the republic, due to the fact that no secondary legislation was adopted actually, played this role of his as a commander in chief throughout the crisis for this entire period. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the deployment of police forces for military purposes is decided, because of the basic principles that any army is organised upon and that is the unity and hierarchy of the command, the police forces that are used in military operations are under the command of the military commanders. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-051, could you agree with me that the decisions of strategic importance are usually issued by the commander in chief and the General Staff, while the corps commanders are usually making operational decisions, while the lower levels of command usually make the decisions of a tactical level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you something completely different now, unrelated to the questions that other persons testified about before this Court. I would like to ask you whether it is correct that the president, as a commander in chief, has in June 2001, adopted a decision about the defence of the city of Skopje, and do you agree with me that such decision was a decision of a strategic nature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, such decision was adopted on the defence of the city of Skopje, and four brigades were established. Now, I could give you their numbers: 12, 6, 8 and 1, I think, 1st Guardist Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask you now to look at -- behind tab 7, a document which is Exhibit 1D949 -- 99.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, Exhibit 1D99. Can you please repeat the document number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 1D99. It is in tab 7. This is a document which is not made public.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-051, you see a document from the president of the Republic of Macedonia, from the 11th of June, 2001, signed by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski. Is this a decision of strategic nature brought by the president about establishing defence command of the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I think that it is a strategic document. Since this is about the capital of the republic, of a state.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in item 2, it lists the brigades which you just also enumerated, which are -- became part of the defence command of the city of Skopje. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. All these brigades are noted here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can agree with me that the defence of the capital always a very important defence task of an army. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the concrete situation, can you agree with me that this was of particular importance in view of the fact that the city of Skopje is located close to the -- bordering southern Serbia and also not far from the border with Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also you could agree with me that in these areas there are -- there was for a longer period of time, a state of crisis, and in 2001, there were terrorist groups and NLA groups, which by way of Skopska Crna Gora, by -- were connecting and coming together through each other nearby Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, via Skopska Crna Gora, Tetovo, Radusa.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at document after -- or in tab 12. This is Exhibit 1D81, and this is 10342 in the Macedonian. And it is English page 1D3048. Have you found this document, Mr. M-051?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is command of the defence of Skopje of the 11th of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And pertains to the defence of the city of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I know this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if you were to look at the last page of this document, 1D3047 and the English version 1D3053, then you could agree that this order was given by Commander General Major Sokol Mitrevski, who was the commander of the defence of the city of Skopje. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We could say, if you agree with me, that after the strategic decision of the president of the republic about the defence of the city of Skopje, that the commander of the defence of Skopje, made an order for the defence of the city of Skopje which was, in effect, an order of operative nature. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Correct. From this order, the order for our brigade was derived. Actually, for the 1st Guardist Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you could concur with me that, in effect, on the basis of this order, in effect, that this order established the mission and the basic task of all bodies which take part in the defence of the city, primarily the army and then police and other bodies. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. It is correct, on the basis of this order we are deployed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you have just said that on the basis on this, the order of the 1st Guardist Brigade was also brought. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the extent of your knowledge there was one defence of Skopje and other bodies did not make or bring decisions but, in effect, joined in and executed the tasks which are listed in this order. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on the basis of this order, is it correct, Mr. M-051, other bodies were obliged to carry out their duties, to plan and to carry out actions so as to carry out the goals and the mission of this order. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes. Everyone would do their part.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When we saw a while back the decision of the president and the order made on its basis, you would agree that this is consistent to your understanding and knowledge of the role of the president as the commander in chief, and giving tasks to army and other bodies for the purpose of the defence. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you -- this decision, to look at the other page of this decision in -- of this order, 1D3043, the English version 3049, I believe. You can see on the top of this page there's item 3, and in paragraph 4, the English version, this is -- item 4 is on the other page, in 3050. No, this is not so. My apologies, let me just have a look. This is 3049, and this is the fourth paragraph of this page, and I would read it out to you. Here it is said: "The forces of the MOI, of MVR blocked the village of Aracinovo and controlled the access points towards the village. With appropriate forces, they secure the facilities of vital importance in the central city area, command post in the MVR facility in Skopje." Do you agree with me, Mr. M-051, that this order and this way of assigning tasks to the Ministry of Interior is practically in accordance with your understanding of the unified command whereby commands of the commander in chief in the joint defence of Skopje are issued through tasks also to the -- units of the Ministry of Interior? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. It is correct the conjunction is mentioned here, joint action. It mentions joint action, in order to prevent deploying army forces at that facility. It is mentioned that police forces will be deployed at the entrance to Aracinovo. So they would then take -- carry out actions at their own level, in order to avoid confusion in the competences between the army and the police so that it does not happen that a facility secured by both army and police, well, there is no need for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at item 5.3 on page 1D3044 and the English version is 1D3050. And here you can see a task of your 1st Guardist Brigade. This tasks, item 2 says that: "With -- supporting upon favour of ground facilities and in joint action with the 12th Brigade and the 8th Ground Brigade and the 1st Brigade and the forces of MVR that are acting within or in that vicinity of the assigned zone to hinder the access of diversion terrorist forces and action upon the central city of Skopje and the organs of Skopje." Do you agree with me if I were to say to you that your brigade had the task of, in effect, together with the Ministry of Interior, act so as to prevent the access of diversion terrorist forces towards the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would ask you to look at the next page, 1D3045, item 8.2. The English version is 1D3051. In this part of the order, the tasks are established of intelligence security, and 8.3, security protection which, in fact, are tasks which you carried out in the brigade. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this item, it is stated that the focus of the intelligence should be on timely notifying of divertive terrorist groups and a gathering information for their deployment strength, arms and direction of movement. And in point 3, it is stated that G3 should secure timely and good quality exchange of information with responsible bodies with the MOI in the area of responsibility. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I see that it is correct. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in relation to this, when you came to that area, you immediately established cooperation with the regional police stations and the units of the Ministry of the Interior in the municipalities that were there, where your brigade was deployed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. We established cooperation with municipality of Georce Petrov, of Cair, with the police station.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, Police Station Cair, Mirkovci and Gazi Baba.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to put to you that when testifying before this Court, the witness Mario Jurisic -- Your Honour, I apologise. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That Mario Jurisic, the commander of the 2nd Company of the 3rd Battalion, testified that he and his soldiers observed immediately upon their arrival significant movements and various elements that showed the presence of the NLA in Ljuboten and around Ljuboten, then you could confirm, corroborate his testimony before this Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I confirm that this is so. I have a lot of information about this movement, which can be seen in the document which I have written myself and sent and (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like ask you to avoid mentioning your post so that we are able to protect your identity, in accordance with the decision of the Chamber while you're testifying here and I will also take care about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it correct that the information spoke the words "people having been seen wearing black uniforms, people -- armed people having been seen," that there were movements around the village during the night, that also some of the cattle was taken to the areas where the NLA was active, also parts of uniforms and ammunition were found in that area, in the direction between the village and the NLA positions, that it was ammunition of Chinese origin, and some were unexpended, live ammunition, which meant that the ammunition was transported through the village, are those the facts that you learned from your subordinates, and, as you stated, also from your personal observations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, everything which you have just said is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that for you a sign that the village of Ljuboten was used as a logistics base for the needs of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: One could say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe, Your Honours, this would be a convenient time for the recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will break now. Could I mention before we do the matter that had been raised by Ms. Motoike. The document marked for identification, 1D85, was marked for identification because there was no translation available of it. One has been provided by the Prosecution and is now incorporated. It would seem that that document should now be received as an exhibit, and that will now happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We -- I gather, there may be some matter, Mr. Saxon, that you need to raise. Ms. Residovic, I'm sure, will excuse you a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, very briefly. It was recently confirmed to me that there has been a glitch, if you will, in the travel plans made for the next scheduled Prosecution witness who was expected to arrive here in The Hague today. Because of this error that was made, not on the part of the Prosecution, this person will not arrive until sometime late tomorrow and therefore will not be available to begin his testimony, as the Prosecution had anticipated at some point during tomorrow's session. So I wanted to inform the Chamber of that, and depending on how long the testimony of the present witness goes, it might be that we are finishing early tomorrow. This error will also have an impact, Your Honours, on the schedule of witnesses for the remainder of the week. The Prosecution had originally intended to bring two Rule 92 bis so-called crime base witnesses to be here to testify on Friday and after consulting with the Defence we agreed that that would now not be realistic and we will only bring one such crime base witness to be here on Friday. It is important that we keep the schedule that we had set for next week because there are two expert witnesses scheduled to come and they have very tight schedules and have made room in their schedules for this Court next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, thank you for that. There's no point for any particular comments about how desirable or undesirable or unfortunate. We accept these things can happen, they have happened. Mr. Mettraux, is there something?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps to assist, Your Honour, we have had an opportunity to discuss the matter of one of the two crime base witnesses which Mr. Saxon has just mentioned and we've also briefly mentioned it to Mr. Saxon. The Defence for Mr. Boskoski and the Defence for Mr. Tarculovski have taken the view that if it is agreeable to the Chamber, we would not insist on cross-examining one of the two crime base witnesses in question which may facilitate the planning of this we can avoid this particular witness having to travel. I'm not sure whether the name of the witness should be mentioned in public session, but if we go into private session I would be happy to do so. In any case, that would be the, I think, the first of the two crime base witnesses to be scheduled for the current week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think there is a need for the Chamber at this point to know the name. The Chamber, and I'm sure, Mr. Saxon are encouraged by what you have said and no doubt discussion between Defence and Prosecution will enable Mr. Saxon to plan the arrival of his witnesses in light of that very helpful comment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In light of that helpful comment, Your Honour, I simply need to emphasise that although the Prosecution is grateful for the expressions by my colleagues on the other side, we may still decide to bring the witness in question that they are referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we have dealt with this matter enough now. I think we move on and we continue to move on as fast as we can with the present witness, because the Chamber is delighted if there is any time available because of other matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-051, prior to the break we were -- or, rather you established that you agree with my assessment that you -- in the brigade and you personally in 2001, had knowledge that the village of Ljuboten is being used as a logistics base for the NLA. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the information which you received in the army of the Republic of Macedonia and in accordance with the order of the command of the city of Skopje, point 8, page 1D3046 and others which we earlier saw, you acquired and received information also from the police bodies about this fact. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The information which the police had was much more comprehensive because the army, in this area, arrived only in June 2001, while the police marked and followed the security state on the ground there for a much longer period of time. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I don't have any written document from the police, since they do not have a duty to communicate information to me in writing. But I confirm this, that when we arrived at these positions in those villages, it was only then that we started gathering information about the movements and the stay there, stay of terrorists or members of other groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the duties which you had in the army, and in view of your present position in the Ministry of Interior, it is clear to you that the questions related to security and observation of the situation was a matter of state and public security or it was called in the Republic of Macedonia, the bureau for security and counter-intelligence. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, we were aware that they were working on those issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you knew that the police earlier and, in particular during the time of the crisis, had regular controls that state control same as military security had associates from among the rank of the Albanians, that for a longer period of time they gathered information about the situation on the ground, and that also they had available operative equipment which enabled them to verify this information.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. I confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at document in tab 15. This is 65 ter 1D510. The Macedonian page, 1D4705; the English 1D4707.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us wait for the document to appear on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you surely found this document in tab 15?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the sake of the transcript, we received this document from the Prosecution according to Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see, Mr. M-051, that this is a document of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, State Security of the 26th February 2001. Is this the document which you're looking at, at the moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, that's the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As of the type of document, we can see that this is a report about a conversation with the position Ljubo, with the operative source Ljubo, these are probably the undercover names with persons with whom state security organs were in contact with. The topic is terrorism and extremism. And in part 2, the content of the meeting: "One can see that, confirming what was -- in confirmation of the above mentioned is the information stated by the source. It was mentioned that not long ago in the old mosque in the village of Ljuboten, during the Dzuma, there were two unknown individuals, according to this speech they were from Kosovo, which publicly informed those present that all kinds of financial aid was needed for the self-style, UCPMB, KLA in terms of finance; and in addition, emphasising that most important is, after all, to have massive joining of people with weapons above 18 years of age and above in the listed organisations --" I will stop reading here. Is this document or does that document show that already in February 2001 there was information about motivation and calling -- villagers from Ljuboten to give logistic support to terrorist diversion groups and that they joined these groups themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes. The document, according to its format, appears to be an Official Note, and it is obvious that there is some operational source with the pseudonym Ljubo, and very similar to the notes that I have written in this sense, and in my opinion, this data is reliable. And I will follow up on this. When I started my intelligence work there, the same people gathered again in that mosque, and I've seen them myself with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at document in tab 16. This is document 65 ter 1D511, page 1D4709 in the Macedonian; and 1D4711 in the English version. And would you agree with me that this is also a document of the state security of Skopje and is an overview of the summary of interesting security-related information which this person came to. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. This is a document --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Source of this document is identical as the previous one, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Can I just add something to this? Such documents, topographic maps with diagrams or some other maps of the city of Skopje I have found myself, as well, when making a search on the grounds in the vicinity of Skopje. And maps -- but also sleeping bags and food were seized and then handed over to my superior officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask you now to turn to the next page of this document. This is 1D4710, or, rather the English version, the same page, last paragraph. And I will read it to you in the Macedonian version where it is stated: "We received information that in the area of Basinec above Ljuboten village, large-scale movement of the population was observed during the day and throughout the night, guards were organised around the installations in the area. It was noticed that a large number of motor vehicles was moving towards Basinec. There are rumours that an unknown number of people are stationed in Basinec waiting to join in the defence of Tanusevci in the event of an intervention by the MVR and ARM. At the entrance of Ljuboten village from the direction of Ljubanci village young men are deployed which guard the entrance of the village and do not let anyone they do not know enter Ljuboten at night." Mr. M-051, does this document also show that in February there were clear information about the activities of NLA and UCK in and around the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes. This document shows it. Since we also had a problem with the village of Tanusevci, and with Brest, Gosince, and a colleague of ours was killed there during an action, and I'm sure that these people were there to help, if help was needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you, Mr. M-051, to look at the document in tab 17 this is document 65 ter, 1D512. Macedonian page 1D4713; English 1D4715. This document would be an Official Note of the state security body, which comes from a conversation with collaborators. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct, yes. It is correct. It is, again, a document, similar to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document was written on the 5th of March, 2001. And in the segment that is labelled content, it is said: "At the state of the meeting, the source presentation information about the activities of individuals in the region of Basinec, in Skopska Crna Gora, and the village of Ljuboten." In paragraph 2, in the last sentence, which begins with: "Also, at the same time, the source stated that some of these individuals regularly go down to the village of Ljuboten, in motor vehicles and also to Skopje. According to him, the frequent movement of motor vehicle on route Basinec-Ljuboten-Skopje is due to the supply of food and other articles for the individuals who are staying there." Is in this last sentence of this paragraph: "As a supplement, the source also said that armed persons were known to descend also to the rest homes at the village of Basinec where the people, refugees from Kosovo of Romani nationality were located." On the other page, 1D4714, in the second paragraph of the Macedonian version, the same page in the English version the next-to-last passage it is said: "With regard to the activities of individual from the village of Ljuboten, the source said that recently, most regularly during the night, young individuals would guard the entrance to the village from the village of Ljubanci. They were unarmed and did not permit entry to the village to unknown individuals." Mr. M-051, is this also a document which clearly shows that the information which you previously confirmed, that much earlier than the deployment of your brigade in the area of Ljuboten, there was knowledge about the presence of NLA in and around the village, and the fact that Ljuboten is being used as logistics base correct? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Since this document is written a bit earlier than my arrival there, but if I look at the actions of the people described here and the explanations in the note, about some movement, supply, especially during the night, I will confirm that this has happened also when we arrived there, at those positions. Also, tractors were used, also the sheep were used as a sort of a disguise. The sheep were taken to the village, but a group of people would come to the village together with the sheep, a larger or a smaller group. I can confirm this. And you can also find it in the reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now ask to you look at the document in tab 18. This is document 65 ter 1D, 1D513 and you will agree with me that is, once again, a report from operative sources in positions known to the main inspector for state security. This is a document 1D4717 in the Macedonian; and 1D4719 of the English version. In the contact under the information, which is given on the 8th of March, 2001, in point 4, Roman numeral IV, third paragraph, it is stated: "With his friend, he and his friend were camouflaged for an extended period of time in one place waiting for any kind of game to pass. However, after a while, the source noticed that a group of four individuals of Albanian nationality from the village of Ljuboten was heading towards them, all between the age of 20 and 25." And in the last passage of this page, which begins with: "In the context of the aforementioned, after around half an hour two unknown individuals arrived with three fully laden horses from the direction of the village of Aracinovo and Rastak and asked the welcoming party if they were carrying was needed and immediately headed towards the village of Ljuboten along the ridge of Skopska Crna Gora in the direction Aracinovo-Tanusevci. There is a passable path which has been in use for some time. On the other page, the English version 1D47278 and English version 1D4720, the passage which begins with: "Further more, the source pointed out that because of the security situation in the country and due to the proximity of the village of Ljuboten from which gun-fire is often heard where the Albanian population lives, the residents of the village of Rastak have come up with the idea of organising their own protection of the population in the case of any problems. However, without any concrete undertakings or fulfilment on -- in the regards to this issue." Mr. M-051, is this document -- does this document also show just all the facts which you testified to looking at the previous documents of the state security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Looking at the document and analysing the description of the localities, the roads, the -- whether the roads could be travelled and also the movement in the directions that were mentioned, I also confirm that this document is reliable, since it has been registered the operational link is mentioned, also the costs for the interview or conversation are also mentioned. I think that this document is a -- this piece of paper deserves attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in view of the relevance of the questions which these documents deal with and the fact that the witness has testified that these facts to him have become known when he arrived at the area, I presume that documents, 65 ter 1D510, 511, 512, and 13 be admitted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honours, with respect to a few of the documents, I believe 1D510 and, perhaps, 1D512 and the last document, 1D513, I believe the witness did attest to its authenticity and as well as to some of the statements contained within. With respect to the additional documents, I don't believe that the witness was able to confirm the reliability of the contents of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying you have no objection to the admission of the three documents you have identified?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: With respect to the other documents, Ms. Residovic, is there anything further you wish to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further explanations other than all of these documents we received from the Prosecution, according to Rule 68, and clearly, they are authentic and the witness, on each of these, confirmed that he believes that these are documents which, so to say, usual, regular, and that his later knowledge confirmed the facts which these documents discuss. I have no further clarification on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The documents will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1D510 will become Exhibit 1D141. 65 ter 1D511 will become Exhibit 1D142. 65 ter 1D512 will become Exhibit 1D143. And 65 ter 1D513 will become Exhibit 1D144, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-051, although you're having looked in these document, you already confirmed the facts, I would now like to ask you: Can you agree with me that in addition to the fact that these documents show the presence of NLA in and around the village of Ljuboten, would it be correct that these documents also lead to the conclusion that, as early as the start of the crisis in Macedonia in 2001, a number of young people from Ljuboten joined the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-051, in view of the fact that in explaining partially your understanding and way of work you confirmed that these and such documents are reliable information, could you agree with me that all officers on the basis of this information, officers of the Ministry of Interior, could rely of the information which security came to, same as military officers in the same manner relied on the information which you verified and submitted to these officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: This is correct. Intelligence and the bureau for security and counter-intelligence relies and believes in its operatives, and all information which are submitted are mostly strictly confidential or are state secret. A piece of information, one information, to be circulated in order for one information to be circulated it needs to be verified from various sides. Therefore, I responsibly answer that these information is reliable and correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The information which we just saw are from the early period of the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia from February and March. Could you agree with me that similar and much more comprehensive information came later and that you also, when you started working in June, also began gathering such information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: The information in regards to the above place, ground, were gathered in March, in April, in May, in June, in July, August, September, up until 2002; while -- when the mobilised reservists were disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In effect, when your brigade was deployed in the area of the Ljuboten and Ljubanci villages and the surrounding villages, the situation in this area was rather complex. Is this not so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very soon after your soldiers, as you just stated earlier, began to find various items such as parts of ammunitions or uniform, tell us, please, is it correct that you frequently found ammunition of Chinese origin which was not used by the army nor by the police of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: This is correct. We found ammunition exactly at Basinec, which you mentioned, in Skopska Crna Gora, in the sheephold of Ardi, which kept sheep there, and during the search of the sheep herd, we found ammunition of Chinese origin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then military security took in certain individuals. You questioned a person called Ismet. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He did not want to speak with you, and he came accompanied by a person by the name of Kenan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Let me clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe we should move into a private session because the witness will probably explain his own activities which could lead to his identity being discovered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-051, you've mentioned Kenan. Do you know that the leader of the village of Ljuboten at that time was Kenan Salievski, or Kenan Saliu?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: According to what I heard, Kenan imposed himself as the head and responsible one for the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was he perceived as a hardliner in the village and is your impression that he was connected to the NLA as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: According to me, frankly speaking, I think he had connection with the persons who were in the village, because he started to impose himself on other people when the crisis began.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, if Kenan Salievski were to say in his statement to the Prosecutor that in the village Baki, or so-called Commander Lisi, was linked to the NLA and that he learned this from Nain Saliu and Rexhep Jusufi with whom Commander Lisi was close, then you would not have any reason to take issue with this fact because certainly Kenan Salievski knew who the other persons connected to the NLA were in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: This is correct. Perhaps he had links but I not researched or investigated this. But can I confirm that he had links. Because the persons which you mentioned are mentioned on that territory after the war too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If also Kenan Saliu would say again in the statement to the ICTY investigator that at least Suad Saliu, Riza Jonuzi, Besim Murtezani, Rafiz Bajrami, Shefajet Bajrami, Fikret Aliu, Nemed Aliu, Ruhan Jashari, Ramadan Jalimi, Musa Selimi, Refedin Selimi, Faik Murati, Shefket Murati, Zaik Murati, Rasim Murati and others whose names he could not mention were NLA in that village, you could again confirm that Kenan Saliu would know who the persons who are NLA members were from that village and that you, also when working there, later would meet or encounter some of these names as being NLA members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I can here confirm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Apologies for the interruption, Your Honour, but I believe the first part of my learned colleague's question asked to confirm knowledge held by another person, in particular Kenan Salievski, which I don't believe this witness can speak to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the problem is largely one of the way the question has been framed, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see, Your Honours, that maybe -- maybe I could break it into two questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: First, Mr. M-051, after I have told you what has Mr. Kenan Saliu stated to the ICTY investigator, to the OTP investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of your person knowledge that Kenan Saliu, considering his position was able to know who from among the villagers were NLA members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I think he knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And my second question, considering that I read to you many names, is it correct also that through your own activities you learned that some of these people were NLA members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I cannot confirm with certainty, but I believe that these persons were mentioned in one place as persons who possibly placed a mine in the military reservists on the 10th of August. Also, I can say that in the village of Ljuboten on the 10th of August, three persons in black uniforms were seen in front of the house of Zendeli in Ljuboten village, which leads me to think that one of the Zendeli family members died.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've mentioned a while ago that you were in communication with the teacher, Dzeljo. Before I continue asking questions, I would like to ask that we move into a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the decision to establish a command for the city, the president, the commander in chief, also ordered call-up mobilisation in the 1st Guardist Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Correct. I believe it was on the 20th of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can agree with me that in the summer 2001, also in August of 2001, most of the members of the 1st Guardist Brigade were members of the reserve forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if the witness Despodov would say before this Court that his battalion had as much as 95 per cent of reserve forces and the witness Jurisic that more than 80 per cent of his company were from the reserve forces these notions would be accurate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Despodov is transcript page 2614 and 2632, and Jurisic transcript page 3353.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And pursuant to the regulation applicable in the army of the Republic of Macedonia, the reserve forces would be replaced every month. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that was a huge obligation on the army and your brigade to develop and train the newcomers from among the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Over such a brief period of time it was very difficult to establish actual real control over some of the reserve forces. Is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: This is correct. There were many undisciplined persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to the OTP and also in your notes, in your log, one can see that the -- some reservists shot a cow in the village of Ljuboten, and this is why you entered discussions with the villagers of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, we had such talks. The cows was taken to a vet. It was checked, it was then killed, slaughtered and the reservist who shot the cow was immediately replaced, or, rather, taken from the village of Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, from the log that you saw, that you have kept over a period of time, but also from other information that you have, we learned that there were other violations of discipline in the battalion and in the brigade, and this is why disciplinary sanctions were taken against the perpetrators, against the offenders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Correct. Rigorous measures were taken against the reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It would happen that celebrating a holiday or for any other unlawful reason they would shoot from their fire-arms and this would be a violation of the discipline.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: They were cases of shooting, of breaking the discipline but measures were taken to have -- to have the ammunition be paid for and --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you stated that these persons were sanctioned and strictly and they would be removed from the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: If they had to be prosecuted, they were prosecuted by the courts. If the problem had not been so severe, the same day they were released from the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But because of the complex situation and the huge number of the reserve forces and their turnover, it happened that many violations went undiscovered. It could have happened. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: There were also cases, but much more rarely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-051, would you agree with me if I say if in a joint action of the army and the members of the MOI where the command belongs to the military commander, a member of the MOI would act in breach of the powers vested in him or would commit a criminal offence even, then the military superior would have the duty to inform the direct superior of his in the Ministry of the Interior so that superior could then take sanctions against the offender, the police officer. Would that be the proper way to act in order to establish responsibility of a police officer participating in the joint action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. If the commander of the army is responsible for the joint action and if somebody makes a disciplinary offence, then the proposal to sanction them would come from the commander, from the immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the military commander would fail to forward this information to the police superior officer, then, of course, the police superior would have no knowledge about the offence that has taken place. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, of course. If that fails ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask to move into a private session again, Your Honours, briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have testified that on the 10th of August at the Ljuboten Bacila there was an explosion of a mine. Is it correct that in this explosion eight people were killed and six members of the army of the Republic of Macedonia were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. Seven were killed, and the 8th one died on the road, when transported to the military hospital, to the army hospital. So it was eight killed and six wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And among the killed were two members of the reserves from the village of Ljubanci, a village neighbouring of the village of Ljuboten. Is this correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct, two reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your soldiers, after the explosion found at the site a substantial number of ammunition and arms. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. There were minutes on that noting the weapons discovered.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at the document after -- on tab 22. This is exhibit 1D86.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would ask that the documents be shown to the public without naming who this document was given to, or rather, without stating where these, all of those items were handed over to --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, whether it is correct that the total -- the ammunition found at the site where the mine exploded was handed by the commander of the 3rd Guard Brigade, Mitre Despodov?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In testifying to this Court, Mitre Despodov said that, in addition to the item listed from 1 to 19 on this list, the explosive means and equipment found, also two documents were handed over, one driving licence and a passport for two persons, inhabitants of Ljuboten. Does this statement remind you that at Ljubotenski Bacila also a driving licence and a passport were -- of two persons from Ljuboten were found?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. The passport, the passports, and the driver's licence, and I think there were some property documents from the land cadastre but there were not sent to be destroyed, since these objects listed here were sent to be destroyed, while the driver's licence and the passports were sent to the sector for intelligence and for security and counterintelligence as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. For the purpose of this transcript Despodov, Witness Despodov spoke about this on page 2663 and 2664. Your understanding was that the surviving soldiers were also shot from the positions of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then members of the army opened fire to the positions of the NLA. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. Fire was opened from the positions and several weapons and instruments were used in that fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me if I were to put it to that you the positions of the NLA from which it was fire were across from the village of Ljuboten, while the positions of the army were above the village of Ljuboten, and that it was possible for the mortars and other grenades that were shot by the NLA towards the position of the army could also hit -- have hit the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I could not confirm this with certainty, but seeing as how they fired at us, since the mines impacted everywhere, it was possible that some of the shells impacted in the village, but I'm not sure about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The investigation about this event was led by the military police of the army of the Republic of Macedonia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. The location of the mine explosion, the investigation, the photographs, the albums, everything was taken care by the army police, and I think I have an Official Note speaking about that day, about what has happened on that date. And the detailed results and the images and the photographs taking on the scene that was done by the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The institute for forensic medicine also carried out post-mortems of the killed soldiers of the army of the Republic of Macedonia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: That is correct. Because I have seen that album in the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Never was one -- either one member of the NLA was not held responsible for this massacre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Thus far, none was held responsible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier, in answering to one of my questions, you said that you had knowledge that on that day on the 8th of August [as interpreted], 2001, three to four armed individuals enter the village, most probably -- which most probably took part in placing the mines. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: That is correct. You can see it from my log, from my notebook. When I received a call from the positions above Ljuboten, that in front of the Zendeli house, the Zendeli family house, three people wearing black uniforms were seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about the 12th of August, you said that in the army barracks Ilinden, you went following the call of Commander Kopacev.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: That is correct. Yes, he called me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And prior to arriving to the command, you did not have any knowledge or any -- of any kind of activities being led in Ljuboten. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. I didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask, Your Honours, in view of the fact that we were going on to the questions, reporting to the statements of the witness to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening, Witness M-051.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I am Antonio Apostolski. I am the lead counsel for Johan Tarculovski. I have with me my co-counsel Jasmina Zivkovic. I wish to tell you before I start my cross-examination that I will ask my questions in Macedonian and that is a language you understand. But still, you should know that my questions and your answers need to be interpreted into several languages, so please do not rush into answering and wait for your answer to be interpreted. Did you understand this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The Skopje Defence Command was composed of four brigades. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 1st Guardist Brigade was stationed to the north of Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct, to the north of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 12th Infantry Brigade was stationed in the eastern area of Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 16th Infantry Brigade was stationed at Vodno hill. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, correct. To the south of Skopje at the hill Vodno.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 8th Infantry Brigade was stationed in the western part of Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. Western part of Skopje towards Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Commander of the Skopje Defence Command was the General Sokol Mitrevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, brigade General Sokol Mitrevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Commander of the 1st Army Brigade was Blazo Kopacev?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, Blazo Kopacev. He was first lieutenant Colonel and then a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Within the 1st Guardist Brigade was also the 3rd Guardist Battalion under the command of Major Mitre Despodov and it was stationed at Skopska Crna Gora mountain. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. It was stationed at Skopska Crna Gora mountain, at the village of Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That was so because there was a risk of the NLA terrorists transferring their actions at the territory of Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The greatest risk came from -- no, I apologise, yes. The greatest risk came from the direction of Skopska Crna Gora mountain, more precisely the direction village Matejce to village Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct. Since behind Skopska Crna Gora mountain there is Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have the assistance of the usher in distributing binders to the Chamber, to the witness, and to my colleagues from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you had information acquired in the course of your work that NLA will attack the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: We had such information, since they spoke publicly, through all media. They would make statements, threats. You know that all NLA commanders were featured on the Internet and anyone could see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have information that Ljuboten could be used as the next location from which NLA will carry out terrorist attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, we had such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter number 2D00-338, which is in tab 2 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see it in front of you? Do you see it on the screen? You have it on the screen, and it is also in tab 2 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see in the upper left corner written: "Security and counter-intelligence administration RO UBK, Prilep?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Give me just a moment to orient myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: No, I apologise. It is UBK, Skopje. OS UBK, Gazi Baba.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: "Type of material, report on meeting with operative source from operative source Vojnik," or soldier in translation. And then it says on page 2, in item 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: From numerous points in the hills of Skopska Crna Gora were NLA reconnaissance points have been placed in order to follow the Macedonian security forces movements on the route between Aracinovo, Stracinci, Cresevo, Bulacani, Rastak, Ljuboten, and first through their physical presence but also later with use of military equipment to intimidate the Macedonian population, that would panic and flee towards Skopje. This would open the corridor Aracinovo-Ljuboten, that in their belief is of multiple significance. It would facilitate the military activities of NLA near Aracinovo. It would greatly facilitate the actions against Skopje, either through classical sabotage terrorist activities or through open military activities. Such corridor would also protect the NLA positions near the monastery of Matejce and through this, also their positions in the villages Otlaj, Matejce, and Vistice. Do this information correspond to the information that you had

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-051
utterances.text: It is correct the information to correspond, especially regarding the villages of Stracinci, Cresevo, Bulacani, Rastak, Ljuboten, that are the positions of my brigade or the 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I if may tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 2D35, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And I think had an is it probably the time, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise. If I may, there's a reference on line 12 of page 86 of today's transcript that I believe should be redacted as it refers to a particular position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will now adjourn and resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of August, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
